Title: May 7, 2026 Boulder City Council Regular Meeting
Overview: The May 7, 2026 Boulder City Council meeting centered on extensive public comment about the tipped minimum wage, a residential vacancy tax, and airport FAA grants, along with a missing and murdered Indigenous persons declaration and several land use items. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda and adopted Ordinance 8741 to designate 745 University Avenue as the Polls and Registration House landmark. It also passed the omnibus land use code amendment, Ordinance 8745, 5-1 with an added provision removing outdoor patio size limits for breweries and tap rooms, and adjourned at 9:42 p.m.

Topic1.Title: Call to order, roll call, and agenda amendment
Topic1.Summary: Council convened the regular meeting and took a roll call with all members present. Council voted unanimously to remove item 4E from the consent agenda, which means the June 11 study session will proceed as usual.

Topic2.Title: Open comment on tipped minimum wage
Topic2.Summary: Multiple residents urged council not to cut the tipped minimum wage, citing the living wage cost in Boulder and the hardship on service workers. Speakers argued that wage cuts would hurt local consumers and the economy and asked council to focus instead on corporate landlords and vacant commercial space.

Topic3.Title: Open comment on residential vacancy tax and housing
Topic3.Summary: Several speakers urged council to place a residential vacancy tax on the ballot and raise the proposed amount from $2,000 to $5,000 per vacant unit. Speakers argued that vacant homes worsen the housing shortage and that a larger tax would be more effective. Speakers also raised concerns about commercial vacancy and tax base erosion.

Topic4.Title: Open comment on Boulder Municipal Airport and FAA grants
Topic4.Summary: Speakers asked council never to accept FAA grants that would commit the city to maintaining the airport in perpetuity. A speaker also criticized an April 23 study session decision to dedicate 175 acres of city land to the FAA and aviation industry, saying the decision relied on unverified information and excluded public input.

Topic5.Title: Open comment on South Boulder Rec Center and other topics
Topic5.Summary: A youth speaker urged council to keep the pool at the South Boulder Recreation Center open, citing the 15-minute city goal. Other speakers raised bike registration, the Charge Bug energy app, an Israel-Gaza divestment request, and concerns about building permit red tape.

Topic6.Title: Staff response and council comments on open comment
Topic6.Summary: Staff said tipped credit changes would come later in the year and that the proposals under consideration would not reduce the tipped minimum wage. Staff committed to follow-up on the lot split question, a health-related concern, and the airport. Council members offered brief comments, including Councilmember Tasha's remarks on a planned July public hearing on tip credit.

Topic7.Title: Consent agenda approval
Topic7.Summary: Council moved and approved the consent agenda, which included items 4A through 4D and 4F through 4L, after clarifying that the beverage licensing rules amendment would be discussed at second reading. The vote was unanimous.

Topic8.Title: National Day of Awareness for Missing and Murdered Indigenous Persons declaration
Topic8.Summary: Council Member Adams presented a declaration recognizing May 5 or 6, 2026 as the National Day of Awareness for Missing and Murdered Indigenous Persons, signed by Mayor Brockett. Speakers from community organizations urged real action beyond proclamations, including policing training, reparations, and caution about Flock camera surveillance harms to Indigenous communities.

Topic9.Title: Call-up check-ins for landmark and site review items
Topic9.Summary: Council reviewed several call-up items, including landmark alteration applications for 409 Mountain View Road and the Chestnut and Arapahoe houses, a height modification at 1039 Mapleton Avenue, and a utility permit at 1420 Cherryvale Road. Council discussed a concept plan for 60 units of permanently affordable senior housing at Presbyterian Manor and decided not to call any items up.

Topic10.Title: Public hearing: Landmark designation of 745 University Avenue
Topic10.Summary: Council held the second reading and public hearing to designate 745 University Avenue as the Polls and Registration House, an individual landmark. The house was a municipal polling place for two decades and was tied to Boulder's early proportional voting history. Council unanimously adopted Ordinance 8741.

Topic11.Title: Public hearing: Omnibus land use code amendment (Ordinance 8745)
Topic11.Summary: Staff presented an omnibus ordinance to fix errors, clarify code, and amend height, use, and site review standards. Changes include removing office floor area limits, allowing height modifications up to 55 feet for certain community uses on three-story buildings, and clarifying parking in converted garages. Council added an amendment removing outdoor patio size limits for breweries and tap rooms, and the ordinance passed five to one.

Topic12.Title: Adjournment
Topic12.Summary: Council closed the meeting at 9:42 p.m. after completing the agenda.
